sources.title: OME-NGFF specification 0.4
sources.applicability: Defines NGFF 0.4/Zarr v2 axes, multiscales, scale/translation transform vocabulary, display hints, and integer image-label conventions. The cited standard does not encode a general rotation/shear affine or the complete application project contract; this does not test any reader.

sources.title: OME-TIFF specification
sources.applicability: Supports interpreting IFD/plane assignments through OME-XML TiffData and DimensionOrder instead of equating TIFF page order with project axes. Specification only; it does not qualify a particular parser.

sources.title: tifffile 2025.5.10 release metadata and description
locators: Use Zarr 2 to read parts of TIFF files
sources.applicability: Release documentation describes TIFF/OME-TIFF support and a regional aszarr route using Zarr 2, with stated compatibility/layout limits. It is documentation, not an executed read or 3 GB performance result.

sources.title: napari stack and channel utilities
sources.applicability: Tagged code wraps direct Zarr arrays in Dask for slicing and routes channel splitting through metadata-aware helpers. This is a component mechanism, not evidence of whole-viewer memory bounds, project persistence or export correctness.

sources.title: napari test_layer_actions.py at v0.6.5
sources.applicability: Regression evidence for the listed RGB-split transform cases only. The Affine wrapper case is translation; the test does not assert general rotation/shear, project persistence or export.

sources.title: napari issue #7085: Split RGB loses affine
sources.applicability: Establishes the reported RGB split failure and environment. It does not establish a fix; patch, PR metadata and tagged test/code are separate sources S7, S8, S4 and S5.

sources.kind: public fix patch with code and test changes
sources.title: napari PR #8256 patch: handle affine layer metadata when splitting RGB images
locators: commit 2b51110: split_rgb uses split_channels and includes rotate/shear metadata
sources.applicability: Patch directly shows the implementation and test change. Its regression cases remain narrower than the rotate/shear handling in the implementation and do not test app persistence/export.

sources.title: napari PR #8256 merge metadata
sources.applicability: Confirms merge and release milestone and explains the old path and intended change. Tagged source and test establish presence in v0.6.5; PR metadata alone is not a test.

sources.title: napari issue #9515: slicing nD Zarr arrays in 2D display over-fetches
sources.applicability: Version-specific report about some local multiscale Zarr slicing. The inline reproducer says napari 0.9.1 and Zarr >=3, while the attached environment reports napari 0.6.1rc1.dev1 and Dask 2026.8.0. No repair is established; do not attribute it to the candidate pins.

sources.title: napari issue #9515 discussion capture
locators: reporter comparison of local Zarr shapes
sources.applicability: Discussion supports read-amplification measurement as a lead. It is not a fix, benchmark, or result for this proposal’s version/configuration.

sources.title: napari v0.6.5 pyproject.toml
sources.applicability: Shows declared constraints/dependencies at the napari tag; does not resolve or test Qt, codecs, operating systems or the complete proposed environment.

sources.title: SQLite Atomic Commit
sources.applicability: Supports a local transactional design subject to filesystem/VFS lock, write and flush assumptions; does not qualify a university network share or artifact/DB cross-resource transaction.

sources.title: OME XML schema June 2016 (OME 2016-06)
sources.pin: OME XML schema namespace 2016-06; schema version 2
sources.applicability: Schema documents distinct pixel spacing, global time increment, per-plane timing and microscope stage positions, including optional unit attributes/defaults. It does not provide a universal oriented affine; a specific parser’s effective-value behavior still needs fixture tests.

sources.title: Zarr Python 2.18.7 release metadata and description
sources.applicability: Release metadata states version 2.18.7, Python >=3.11 and runtime requirements including numcodecs. It supports the candidate pin intersection only; it does not establish integration or performance.
